message: tag-check (bin/tag-check.py) lints the Obsidian vault's tags against an allowlist of BRANCHES, not exact tags: a branch covers everything under it, so new sub-tags cost nothing and only a new top-level tag is flagged. Why: every junk tag so far (Bear importer filing '#1' as a tag, a notes-synthesis tool writing 14 tags as a YAML flow list) landed at the top level, and an exact-tag list would punish making a tag on purpose. Report-only by design; answers to a stranger are --allow (new branch) or --ignore (hashtag left in note text). The list lives in the vault at .obsidian/tag-roots.txt, not in this repo: script = mechanism, list = the vault's private policy. Python, not bash like jd-check, because it has to parse YAML frontmatter shapes and Markdown code fences. Rejected: an Obsidian plugin (couples the check to the app), auto-stripping (could delete an intentional tag).

tag-check must count a tag exactly the way Obsidian does or it gets ignored. Two traps found building it: (1) hashtags inside fenced or inline code are NOT tags. A first census that skipped this reported 20 caption hashtags as live inline tags when all sat in code blocks in 3 notes; the importer had only copied them into Properties. Fences need the real Markdown rule (close only on a bare line of the same char, at least as long; unclosed runs to EOF), not a toggle. (2) Properties tags arrive as block list, flow list, wrapped flow list, scalar, or under the singular key 'tag'; a parser that knew only block lists saw nothing in a generated note. Digit-only tags count in Properties but not inline. test-tag-check.sh pins each case; mutation-checked by breaking flow lists, the branch-slash match, and fence skipping.

pebbl init in this repo (2026-10-06) replaced the existing .git/hooks/pre-commit (397 bytes, installed 2026-07-29) with the current pebbl privacy-scan hook, with no backup, and added post-commit, post-merge, post-checkout and pre-push hooks plus AGENTS.md and .gitattributes. 'pebbl init --help' mentions none of the hooks. Git history (16d107f, 11a77f5) indicates the old hook was an earlier pebbl privacy-scan, so the job is preserved, but the old bytes are unrecoverable. Before running pebbl init in any repo, copy .git/hooks aside first.

Obsidian theme (obsidian/themes/Bear Graphite) is COPIED into the vault by bin/obsidian-theme.sh, the one exception to this repo's symlink-everything rule. Why: the vault lives in iCloud and the phone reads it; iCloud does not follow a symlink out of the vault, and a .git folder inside iCloud gets corrupted, so neither a symlink nor a repo inside the vault works. The repo is the source: edit here, --install, commit. Default mode is a report-only compare (exit 1 on drift) so a stale copy is visible; --pull brings a vault-side edit back. Tag icons stay out of the repo: they are Notebook Navigator settings keyed by private tag names, same split as tag-check (mechanism here, private list in the vault). Not done: no test-obsidian-theme.sh yet, no README section, not wired into check-dev-tools-health.sh.

dev-tools' own pebbl store switched from local to SHARED mode (pebbl init --shared) on 2026-10-07 so its memory is committed and pushed to the private GitHub repo: Ashley wants the memory tracked with the repo, same as ~/pebbl. events.jsonl is the committed source of truth; db.sqlite, view.sqlite and the .md projections stay local and rebuild from it. Checked before switching: all 9 logs and 4 commits in db.sqlite were already in events.jsonl, so nothing is hidden by reading from the fold. GOTCHA: on a store that was first set up with plain pebbl init, init --shared adds the named ignores and a !.pebbl/events.jsonl negation but leaves the old blanket .pebbl/ line, and git does not look inside a blanket-ignored directory, so events.jsonl stayed ignored until that line was removed by hand. Open: nothing commits events.jsonl automatically here (the pebbl repo has a daily job), and the post-commit hook appends a commit event after every commit, so the file is usually one event ahead of git.

Bear Plum (obsidian/themes/Bear Plum) is a full-copy fork of Bear Graphite for palette experiments: only color lines differ, so a diff of the two theme.css files shows just the palette. Why a copy: an Obsidian theme is one theme.css with no imports, so sharing the layout rules needs a build step or moving palettes into CSS snippets; not worth it until a second palette is kept for good. Gotcha for any light accent: under .theme-dark Obsidian (1.14.4 app.css) sets --text-accent to --color-accent-1, which is the accent at lightness x1.15, and accent-2 at x1.29. An accent at 79% lightness draws links near 90%, next to the normal text color, so Bear Plum pins --text-accent to --color-accent. The sidebar is darker than the editor, so base-20 sits below base-00 and the Notebook Navigator selected rows point at base-30 (#522b5b) where Bear Graphite uses base-40. Heading color #c2a5fe was picked in OKLCH: the editor color's hue 298.7 at lightness 0.78 with chroma near the sRGB limit. #854f6c is 2.6:1 on the editor, so faint text is #b2838f. State 2026-10-07: installed in the vault, uncommitted, not yet viewed rendered by an agent because notes are private.

Bear Plum (obsidian/themes/Bear Plum) is a full-copy fork of Bear Graphite for palette experiments: only color lines differ, so a diff of the two theme.css files shows just the palette. Why a copy: an Obsidian theme is one theme.css with no imports, so sharing the layout rules needs a build step or moving palettes into CSS snippets; not worth it until a second palette is kept for good. Gotcha for any light accent: under .theme-dark Obsidian (1.14.4 app.css) sets --text-accent to --color-accent-1, which is the accent at lightness x1.15, and accent-2 at x1.29. An accent at 79% lightness draws links near 90%, next to the normal text color, so Bear Plum pins --text-accent to --color-accent. Surfaces: editor, note list and sidebar all use #190019 (base-00 = base-20). First try had the editor at #2b124c; Ashley saw it live and found it too bright for a page of text, so #2b124c moved to code blocks (base-10). Notebook Navigator selected rows point at base-30 (#522b5b) where Bear Graphite uses base-40. Heading color #c2a5fe was picked in OKLCH: the hue of #2b124c (298.7) at lightness 0.78 with chroma near the sRGB limit. #854f6c is 3.2:1 on #190019, so faint text is #b2838f. To switch the live theme without the UI: edit cssTheme in the vault's .obsidian/appearance.json; Obsidian watches that file and reloads the theme. State 2026-10-07: installed in the vault and active, uncommitted.
